_comment: MultiHitBoxLib hitbox profile for orespawn:spider_robot (2.0 S4).
MODERN-GAIT ONLY: SpiderRobot implements ICustomHitboxProfileSupplier
and returns Optional.empty() for classic-mode spiders (construction
snapshot), so this profile only ever builds parts for modern spiders.
No synched bones and sync-with-model=false: these parts are fed
SERVER-SIDE by the gait solver (ModernSpiderGait positions each part
on its leg's lower-segment midpoint every tick; the client mirrors
locally from the replayed solve). The GeckoLib bone-collection path,
bone packets and client trust are entirely uninvolved.
main-hitbox size — THE LAW (general rule): the profile main size
must equal the classic EntityType dims EXACTLY. MHLib applies the
profile main size through its EntityEvent.Size hook, so a
profile/EntityType mismatch silently forks modern dims from
classic. Both sit at [3.25, 2.25] = orig SpiderRobot.java:58
setSize (ENT-S-088 restored them; port 1.0 had shipped a shrunken,
never-audited 2.0x1.5). Drift in EITHER mode is pinned by
s4_part_counts_and_classic_zero; the ant's s5b/i083 pins guard the
same contract family. canReceiveDamage=true keeps the BODY pickable and
damageable (design D3: legs are additional honest surfaces, never a
forced routing like the Queen's).
Legs: damage-modifier 1.0 (no new weak points), non-collidable
(classic legs never collided; pickability comes from the S4
isPickable fix: collidable OR can-receive-damage),
max-deviation-from-server 0 (no client authority).
Accepted honest-surfaces delta vs classic (review-recorded): melee
and projectiles on legs deal body-identical damage, but an
explosion near a foot now damages by the closest of NINE surfaces
(max-not-sum via the parent hurt cooldown) — a strictly larger
blast profile than classic's body-only box. Environmental
(source-less) damage NEVER routes through legs (S4 lava rule):
the environment acts on the body, which can receive damage
directly on this profile.
